title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard speaks out in first interview about partner's death

 Brendan Morrow USA TODAY Updated Nov. 16, 2026, 10:39 a.m. ET Hear this story Gypsy Rose Blanchard is speaking out in her first interview since the death of her partner Ken Urker .
 Blanchard said she is "still trying to process everything" and "can't make sense of anything anymore" in a conversation with "60 Minutes Australia," more than a month after Urker died in October on his 34th birthday from an accidental drug overdose . She described saying "no, no, no, no, no, no, no, this isn't true, you're lying" after hearing the news.
 "I just hit the floor, and I just remember screaming, screaming, screaming, screaming, 'No, no, no,'" she said.
 The Lafourche Parish Sheriff's Office in Louisiana previously confirmed to USA TODAY that it responded to a call to a home on Oct. 1 at 6:15 p.m., where Urker was found dead. "To this point in the investigation, we have found no evidence of foul play," the office said.
 According to an incident report, police found "paraphernalia," including syringes and a spoon, in the bathroom of the residence. The items were located next to a "brown powdery substance," and a syringe and handgun were seen on Urker's nightstand. Blanchard told People magazine that Urker died from an apparent overdose.

 Gypsy Rose Blanchard speaks out on death of Ken Urker. What we know Blanchard spent more than eight years in prison after being convicted of assisting in the 2015 murder of her abusive mother, Clauddine "Dee Dee" Blanchard. In the "60 Minutes Australia" interview, Blanchard slammed "disgusting" online speculation that she had something to do with her partner's death.
 Gypsy Rose Blanchard's partner Ken Urker dead at 34 "That was the love of my life," she said. "That's the father of my child. I've known Ken for almost nine years. No other man, no other person, had my heart like he did."
 Blanchard and Urker, who became pen pals while she was in prison, welcomed their daughter, Aurora Raina Urker, in December 2024.
 Ken Urker cause of death released Blanchard also said that Urker struggled with online scrutiny over their relationship and spiraled after their prison calls were made public. In October, she launched a campaign to pass a law to combat online bullying in honor of Urker.
 "We're talking [about] people that monetize off of creating rumors for clicks and views, without any regard to how that affects those individuals' mental health," she told "60 Minutes Australia," adding that her message to online trolls is, "I hope that someone doesn't do this to your loved one."
 In October, Blanchard shared a statement with TMZ confirming her partner's death, saying at the time that "Ken was an amazing father and a man who was deeply loved." She added that he "will forever be my soulmate and my red string, a connection that time, distance, and even death can never erase."
